clue.text: Black bird in hollow

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a nocturnal bird of prey

explanation.surface: A dark bird sits tucked away in a dip in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl is a rounded depression or basin, so a hollow in the landscape can be called one.

clue.text: Second bull in game

blocks.note: to second a proposal is to back or support it
bull and gammon are both slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: A runner-up bull at an agricultural show or a bullfight game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a position in a contest but is the verb meaning support; 'bull' is short for nonsense, as is the old slang gammon.
explanation.definitionFit: Backgammon is a board game for two players moving counters by dice throws.

clue.text: Terribly weird, prince's new mechanically operated cleaning device

indicators.note: something done terribly is done badly, so the following letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prince's strange new cleaning gadget is described as terribly weird.
explanation.walkthrough: All fifteen letters of 'weird, prince's new' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A windscreen wiper is a motorised arm that sweeps rain and dirt off a car's front glass.

clue.text: What's always displayed in Tiffany's?

blocks.note: surface reading: the jewellery permanently on show at the famous New York store
setter's reading: the written name itself, which always shows a punctuation mark before the final s

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders what the jeweller Tiffany's keeps permanently in its windows.
explanation.walkthrough: Think of the word Tiffany's on the page rather than the shop: the mark before the s is always there.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive form of a name is written with this punctuation mark, so it appears in every printing of the store's name.

clue.text: City — relax in quiet one out East

indicators.note: out means removed, so the compass letter is dropped from the word before it
in places the relaxing word inside the letters around it

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
to rest is to relax
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A traveller unwinds quietly in a city while someone heads off eastwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The relaxing word sits between the quiet letter and what is left of one. Preston is a city in Lancashire, north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Preston is a city in Lancashire in north-west England, granted city status in 2002.

clue.text: Post over in Special Air Service could cause distress

indicators.note: in a down clue over means flipped upside down, so the word is turned round
in puts the turned word inside the regiment's abbreviation

blocks.note: to post a letter is to send it
the initials of the British special forces regiment

explanation.surface: A posting with the SAS special forces regiment could bring someone real anguish.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' turns the word upside down. The SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadness is sorrow or unhappiness, a close synonym for distress in the emotional sense.

clue.text: Girl in race, one over a fictional land

indicators.note: in means the girl's name is placed inside the word for a race

blocks.note: a run is a race
a girl's name
Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl runs in a race in some made-up country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' is positional: in a down answer the numeral sits above the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruritania is the imaginary central European kingdom of Anthony Hope's novel The Prisoner of Zenda.

clue.text: Popular run for buses etc.

blocks.note: popular in the sense of of the people, public
to run goods or people somewhere is to transport them

explanation.surface: A well-used route for buses and similar vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Buses, trains and trams are the standard examples of shared transport systems open to everyone.

clue.text: Garden gnome finally found on site

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: the final letter of gnome
a den is a site or lair where an animal lives

explanation.surface: A garden gnome turns up on the premises.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'found on' places the letter above the word for site.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the biblical Garden in which Adam and Eve were placed.

clue.text: Some unfortunate fish

indicators.note: some means only part of the following word is used, lying inside it

blocks.note: the letters run consecutively inside the word

explanation.surface: Some fish are unlucky ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large ocean fish widely caught for food.

clue.text: PC, losing little time, nicks upper-class murder suspect in a car?

indicators.note: losing means the time letter drops out of the police officer
suspect means dubious or unreliable, so the letters are not in their proper order
to nick is to arrest or catch, so the officer holds the other letters inside

blocks.note: PC stands for police constable
T is the abbreviation for time
U is the old label for upper-class usage
taken as written

explanation.surface: A police officer arrests a posh murder suspect in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nicks' reads as arrests in the surface and works the same way in the wordplay, holding the jumbled letters. The question mark flags a car as just one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is a typical consumer durable: a household purchase expected to last several years rather than be used up.

clue.text: Mesh cover left inside gets a man mad

indicators.note: inside means the left letter is placed within the jumbled words
mad means crazy or deranged, so the words before it are scrambled

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man is driven mad by being stuck inside a mesh covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas mantle is the fine fabric mesh fitted over a gas lamp's flame, glowing white when heated.

clue.text: Helpful hint about river excursion

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hint goes around the river letter

blocks.note: a tip is a useful piece of advice
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone offers useful advice about a boat outing on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a short journey or outing, the same thing as an excursion.

clue.text: Unexpectedly attacked French novelist over stole

blocks.note: George Sand, the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin
to bag something is to take or steal it

explanation.surface: A French writer was ambushed and had something taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' could be the scarf, but it is the past tense of steal. In a down clue 'over' puts the novelist above.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sandbagged is to be ambushed or caught off guard, originally by a blow from a bag of sand.

clue.text: Sci-fi character? Deface one cast in bronze

indicators.note: cast in means thrown inside, so the numeral is put within the colour word

blocks.note: to mar is to spoil or deface
a bronze or tan is a suntan colour
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A science-fiction figure gets defaced: a statue cast in bronze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast in bronze' reads as metalworking, but the numeral is simply placed inside TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Martians, beings from Mars, are stock characters of science fiction, as in The War of the Worlds.

clue.text: Imply wrongdoing in a unit, possibly by leader of expedition

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters are rearranged
in places the wrongdoing word inside the rearranged letters
the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a sin is a wrongdoing
the first letter of expedition

explanation.surface: Someone hints that misconduct has occurred in a unit, perhaps by its expedition leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imply wrongdoing' reads as one phrase, but only 'Imply' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To insinuate is to suggest something indirectly, usually something unpleasant, which is what implying does.

clue.text: Singer sat entertaining popular artist

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them, so the word sat holds the next one

blocks.note: taken as written
something in is fashionable or popular
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A singer sat performing for a well-known painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra was the celebrated American crooner of songs such as My Way.

clue.text: What supervisor did about cutting tool?

blocks.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money
a saw is a toothed cutting tool

explanation.surface: A question about what a foreman did with a saw.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor's job is to watch over work, so in the past tense the supervisor oversaw it.

clue.text: Fiddle involving rupees causes angry argument

indicators.note: involving means including, so the fiddle word takes the currency letter inside it

blocks.note: to wangle is to fiddle or obtain by trickery
R is the abbreviation for rupees, Indian currency

explanation.surface: A financial fiddle involving Indian money leads to a furious row.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrangle is a long, heated dispute, so it matches an angry argument.

clue.text: After parking, young man goes round vehicle to get what may be carried in a demo

definitions.text: what may be carried in a demo

indicators.note: goes round means encircles, so the young man surrounds the vehicle

blocks.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a lad is a young man
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A young man parks and walks around his car before joining a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Protesters at a demonstration carry placards, boards bearing slogans.

clue.text: Greek philosopher arranged to supply a small body of soldiers

blocks.note: Plato, the ancient Athenian philosopher
an arranged event is on, as in the game is on

explanation.surface: An ancient philosopher arranges supplies for a small army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' looks like an anagram signal, but it simply gives the word for scheduled.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a small military unit, a subdivision of a company commanded by a lieutenant.

clue.text: Double thread cut off at the end

indicators.note: cut off at the end means the final letter is removed

blocks.note: twine is strong thread or string

explanation.surface: A doubled thread has been snipped at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin is an exact counterpart, as is a double or lookalike.

clue.text: Treated as a saint, a grand duchess

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grand duchess is venerated as a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: the Russian Orthodox Church canonised the Romanov family.
explanation.definitionFit: Anastasia Romanov was a grand duchess, the youngest daughter of the last Russian tsar.

clue.text: Changed course, we hear, as a measure of diplomacy?

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by its spoken sound, not spelling

blocks.note: a sailing boat that tacks changes course against the wind

explanation.surface: A diplomat changes direction as a matter of diplomacy.
explanation.walkthrough: Tacking is the sailing term for turning into the wind to change course.
explanation.definitionFit: Tact is sensitivity in dealing with people, the core skill of diplomacy.

clue.text: Female cut in crash

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A woman is injured in a road accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal but just joins the parts to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flop is a failure, as a crash can be in business or the theatre.

clue.text: Drink of rum punch? A glass? Go on!

indicators.note: rum in British slang means odd or strange, so the following letters come out oddly ordered

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring punctuation

explanation.surface: Someone at a party is urged to have a glass of rum punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the spirit in the punch, but it is the old British word for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapsang souchong is a smoky black tea from China, so a drink, ironically far from rum punch.

clue.text: See pout by French river in net?

blocks.note: to purse the lips is to pout
the river that runs through Paris

explanation.surface: Someone sulks beside a French river, perhaps over a fishing net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is an imperative pointing at the wordplay; PURSE is placed beside SEINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A purse seine is a large fishing net drawn closed at the bottom like a drawstring bag.

clue.text: Boss demanding endless attention

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the last letter is removed

blocks.note: study is close attention to something

explanation.surface: A bossy manager constantly wants attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is the noun for a raised knob, not a manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a round ornamental knob, as on a shield, and a stud is a similar raised stud or knob.
